question:
Neutron separation energy is defined as the energy required to remove one neutron from a nucleus:

$S_n(A,Z)=\big[M(A-1,Z)+m_n-M(A,Z)\big]c^2.$ Given atomic masses: $M(^{56}\!Fe)=55.934936\,u$, $M(^{55}\!Fe)=54.938293\,u$, and $m_n=1.008665\,u$.
Also given: $m_H=1.007825\,u$ and $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$. (a) Calculate the neutron separation energy $S_n$ for $^{56}\!Fe$.
(b) Interpret physically what the value of $S_n$ implies about the energy released in the capture process $^{55}\!Fe + n \rightarrow ^{56}\!Fe + \gamma$ (neglect recoil).
(c) Using binding energy from atomic masses, verify that \[S_n = BE(^{56}\!Fe)-BE(^{55}\!Fe).\] (d) Evaluate the statement: “A large $S_n$ indicates that the last neutron is strongly bound and the nucleus is resistant to neutron emission.”

options.A: $S_n\approx 11.20\,\text{MeV}$; neutron capture releases $\approx 11.20\,\text{MeV}$; and $S_n=BE_{56}-BE_{55}$ is verified, so the statement is correct
options.B: $S_n\approx 1.12\,\text{MeV}$; neutron capture releases $\approx 1.12\,\text{MeV}$; and $S_n\ne BE_{56}-BE_{55}$, so the statement is incorrect
options.C: $S_n\approx 112\,\text{MeV}$; neutron capture releases $\approx 112\,\text{MeV}$; and the statement is correct
options.D: $S_n\approx -11.20\,\text{MeV}$; neutron capture must absorb energy; and the statement is incorrect
